tweets.text:
Brian Armstrong tells the story of suing Gary Gensler's SEC

"When you go public you have to describe every single detail of your business to the SEC. They turned over every stone, and then they allowed us to become a public company. Then a year later, Gensler's SEC came to us saying they were concerned about everything we were doing"

"I said, you're the regulator just tell us what the rules are and we're happy to comply. Gensler told me, I'm not going to give you legal advice, you need to talk to your lawyers"

"People said as a public company CEO you should never sue the SEC, it'll put a cloud over your company for years. But our alternative was shutting down the whole industry in the US. At some point I was like, screw it we've got to push back"

"We sent a FOIA request for Gary Gensler's text messages. After many rounds of negotiation the SEC came back and said he had accidentally deleted them. They can't find them"

"If the government is suing you as a public company CEO and you say, oh yeah I accidentally deleted all the documents.. you'd pay a $100 million fine"

"But anyway, in this case the court actually ruled in our favor and censured them and told them that they had violated their obligations and actually awarded us damages"
tweets.title: Brian Armstrong tells the story of suing Gary Gensler's SEC

tweets.author: @MarketBubble
tweets.text:
Brian Armstrong explains why he got into crypto

"I'm super into freedom and economic freedom. There's so many people around the world who get their wealth eroded from them by inflation, or they're getting nickel and dimed on fees to just store their money securely, to move it around.. basic property rights"

"I'm an investor, but I'm not an active day trader. That's actually a weakness of mine. When I co-founded Coinbase with Fred Ehrsam, he was a trader coming from Goldman Sachs. We had both sides of it"

"I initially got into crypto thinking this is going to be a global payment system where everything is fast and cheap and cross-border. We are seeing that now with stablecoins, which is really cool but the trading stuff is just as important"

"Even if my day sucks and I got yelled at, and the people in DC are telling me I'm an idiot, or Jamie Dimon hates me, whatever it is. We've got to go create more economic freedom in the world. That's what keeps me getting out of bed in the morning"
tweets.title: Brian Armstrong explains why he got into crypto

tweets.author: @MarketBubble
tweets.text:
Brian Armstrong tells the full Coinbase origin story

"In 2010 I read the Bitcoin white paper. I was living in SF, I was an early software engineer at Airbnb and I was trying to help them move money all over the world. I read that white paper and I was like wow this is really powerful"

"It's kind of like the internet.. global, decentralized, but instead of for moving information around, it's for moving money. I was like this would be amazing if the world had this open financial system"

"I started going to these early Bitcoin meetups in SF. Tradehill was around at that time, Mt. Gox was there at that time. And I remember thinking oh maybe I'm too late. Maybe I missed my shot"

"Y Combinator gave me the first $150K check. That convinced me: all right I'm going to quit my job and really go for this. Most of the early days was just trying to get anybody to care about the app whatsoever"

"We had amazing fundraise rounds where everybody wanted to invest. We had terrible fundraise rounds where we were desperate to just get one term sheet. Eventually went public in 2021, a cool 10 year journey"
tweets.title: Brian Armstrong tells the full Coinbase origin story

Ansem breaks down the two ways to make a lot of money trading

"In trading, there are two ways you make a lot of money. The first is by seeing around corners, finding a fundamental thesis the market doesn't see yet, where the general consensus is against it, and betting on that early and with size"

"Once the market shifts from something being non-consensus to consensus, that's when everybody who wasn't allocated starts allocating towards that idea. You make a lot of money because you were one of the first to have it"

"The second way is learning to ride momentum and trade the consensus ideas before they top. When an idea becomes consensus, it usually stays consensus for a certain amount of time"

"Don't try to buy the bottom, don't try to sell the top, try to catch the meat in the middle"
